decisions.reason: As a flagship product shown on the home page and tightly aligned with the firm's strategic move toward cloud-based enterprise messaging, it likely met aspirations well enough that a growing, hiring firm with R&D slack would continue it.
Its dedicated page and explicit customer reference suggest satisfactory market acceptance relative to aspirations, so management would have little reason to reallocate resources away from it.

Although only lightly evidenced on the website, it builds on the established messaging offer and likely uses existing capabilities, which lowers pressure to drop it in a firm with some organizational slack.

This feature sits close to the core fax-delivery business and is probably inexpensive to maintain, but its limited prominence and narrower legacy-channel relevance make it more vulnerable than the stronger products.
Threat protection fits the firm's compliance and security positioning in a growing market, so despite modest visible evidence management would likely retain it while continuing to learn about demand.
